summary: Submitted a sourced 'explained' Candidate closing the leadership-transfer surface (action=explained), which the map had only as a deferred high-consequence surface. The question selects F-leadership's establishment lifecycle through B-election, with B-authority-loss as context, and asks three concrete things about the provoked election. Each is answered by a read mechanism rather than a check: (1) leadershipTransfer sends TimeoutNow only after the target's nextIndex has passed the leader's last index, so the target has acknowledged every entry the old leader held and its log is at least as up to date as any voter's; (2) leaderLoop rejects Apply/Barrier/configuration requests while leadershipTransferInProgress is set, and the flag is cleared only when the transfer goroutine finishes or times out, so no client write can be dispatched and then be missing from the new leader; (3) requestVote still enforces configuration membership (inConfiguration), voter suffrage (hasVote), the persisted one-vote-per-term rule and the log up-to-dateness check even though the LeadershipTransfer flag suppresses the known-leader rejection, so a non-voter or removed server cannot win. Counterevidence is the sourced mechanism itself, the answer keeps the residual limit explicit (TimeoutNowRequest carries no term, so a replayed TimeoutNow cannot be distinguished; its consequence is not settled), and the question cites acquired Materials for the transfer, election and vote paths. No defect is presumed and no map object changes. Preflight returned valid:true; the run's four confirmed_in_scope conclusions across five implementation_reproduced findings stand unchanged.
